greyscale.description: Greyscale panels; 8-bit + render resampling limit r to ~0.99, equal to mutual brain correlation

error_panel.description: Error |rec-gt| / max(gt_volume) through jet [0,0.1]; fixed range, never autoscaled

calibration_stake.description: Positive/negative control stake (replaces the fix-round-2 self-comparison tautology, which called _render_error_panel twice with identical arguments and so was r=1.0 by construction). positive = best candidate's error map rendered at the claimed true slice vs the REAL extracted panel 3; negative = same candidate's error map rendered at a clearly different slice (control), vs the same real panel. Passes iff positive beats negative -- no absolute threshold; the negative control IS the reference.

note_uniqueness_ceiling: Fix round 1 (M2): two DIFFERENT things block `resolved`, not one uniform ceiling issue as an earlier version of this note implied. The greyscale reading's top_correlation=0.9917 actually CLEARS the top>0.99 bar; it fails only on gap=0.0003 (<0.01 -- the top-5 candidates are near-identical tv_eps neighbours). The error_panel reading's top_correlation=0.9680 is the one that misses the top>0.99 bar, and it sits below this pipeline's own measured extraction ceiling: the greyscale GT self-calibration reads r_top=0.9893 (< 0.99) even when the reconstruction shown IS the true source, because 8-bit PNG quantisation + bilinear resampling cap the achievable correlation. Both are documented limitations of the reading (rules registered pre-data are not adjusted post-hoc); neither changes the criterion or the unique_match/resolved verdict.
